title: Normalize shifts of the explicit common-field adjunction
statement: Fix a prime l, an algebraic closure Ω of Padic l, a finite-field datum D with l ≠ D.p, finite-type quasi-compact D.k-schemes X and Y, and a separated finite-type quasi-compact D.k-morphism f : X → Y. Let A be RingStageAssembly l Ω D hl for f [def-sf-ring-stage-assembly-data], and P a RationalStageAssembly over A [lem-sf-rational-stage-localization]. No absolute separatedness is assumed. Let L_c, R_c and a_c be the explicit rationalCommonLeft.functor, rationalCommonRight.functor and rationalCommonAdjunction [lem-sf-rational-common-scalar-coherence]. There exist integer CommShift structures on the endpoint common-field inclusion functors, chosen independently of c, and on L_c and R_c, such that L_c and R_c are triangulated, the actual unit and counit of a_c commute with shifts, and the inverse canonical stage-restriction isomorphisms for L_c and R_c commute with shifts using the original P.operation shifts. This is Nonempty RationalCommonShiftData. No functor, adjunction, comparison map or transition equation is an existential output.

source.place: Construction 6.6, common-field descent step 4 only: endpoint shift normalization and exactness after explicit unshifted descent.

proof.text: Take the ratio of each supplied endpoint localization shift with the canonical one. Residue Tor gives integral representatives of every rational object. Naturality on integral arrows extends to all rational arrows, which are sums of scalar multiples of localized integral arrows; scalar multiplication commutes with all morphisms. This descends the ratios and their zero/addition laws to natural automorphisms of the rational shifts. P.shiftX and P.shiftY make them independent of compactification. The identity localization q and its shift square express the original left shift through these endpoint corrections and the integral shift normalized by A.leftShift. Apply the endpoint corrections to the canonical inclusion shifts. With no compactification all c-indexed claims are vacuous.

Transport the canonical compact-support shift through P.left. The normalized integral scalar comparison and its shift square, followed by P.scalar_normalized, prove scalar compatibility of these normalized rational shifts. Obtain the right shift by adjunction transposition. Descend both normalized shift families to the actual pair functors; on representatives the scalar squares prove naturality, and on objects the finite zero/addition laws prove the CommShift laws. Transport the endpoint corrections back in the restriction squares to recover exactly the original rational left shift; uniqueness of the adjoint shift recovers the original right shift and bShift.

Use canonical inclusions and normalized finite shifts for exactness: every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to an included finite-stage triangle, whose image under the normalized compact-support functor is distinguished. The triangulated-adjunction theorem makes the right adjoint exact. The descended unit and counit are the included finite maps, so their finite shift squares prove the remaining shift compatibilities. This supplies exactly RationalCommonShiftData.
